newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity moves higher in thin volume.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity moves higher in thin volume.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading mostly higher in thin volume that traders said was mostly range-bound with a lack of fundamentals to move the market.
"The volume is very, very thin so I wouldn't read all that much into the upward movement," said one New York based futures broker.
NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures were also trading higher, with December up about 1.2 cents at near $2.765 per million British thermal units.
In the West, Bonneville Power Administration said it was not offering surplus power for Friday schedulings.
As of 1200 EDT, December California Oregon Border (COB) had traded up 20 cents at $23.70 but was being bid at $23.75 after trading as high as $24.10 per megawatt hour (MWh).
January COB traded steady at $21.00 per MWh.
December Palo Verde (PV) had traded up 10 cents at $21.90 after exchanges as high as $22.20, while January had traded up 30 cents at $19.80 per MWh.
Remaining PV deferreds were mostly being bid and offered above Wednesday's closes.
October, November and December 1997 PV had all traded once at new contract highs.
NYMEX said that as of 1135 EST, an estimated total of 34 COB and 57 PV contracts had traded.
